newsitem.title: UK: No revolution, no wild promises - UK Labour's Blair.
newsitem.headline: No revolution, no wild promises - UK Labour's Blair.

text.p: Tony Blair, leader of Britain's main opposition Labour party, said on Tuesday he would promise nothing in the general election campaign that he could not deliver if he won power.

"We do not promise a revolution. We promise a government which can bring the country togther, heal the divisions of the past and look to the future with confidence," Blair told his opening news conference of the campaign.
"We promise only what we will deliver, and we will deliver what we promise," Blair, whose party holds a lead of about 25 percentage points in the run-up to the May 1 ballot, said.
"The choice in this election is clear: between an old, tired discredited Tory party and New Labour, a party true to its values but reborn for a new age," Blair added.
